video_note: 16:9 master, 82.1 s (take 80.64 s + ~1.5 s tail), 1920x1080, 30 fps. The only cut; no 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 timeline exists.
character: One dry Kiwi narrator telling the whole thing over the live pages (Cam S, ElevenLabs voice 53CG2aO2HU48thT3QnMl). General NZ accent, never a caricature, no announcer lift, no exclamation marks; the hook bold, the thread weary, the German self-own amused, the product lines plain, the honest bit straight. Continuous speech: the narration never stops for more than 1 s except the deliberate 'Leistungs…' beat.

take.method: ONE unbroken request to /v1/text-to-speech/53CG2aO2HU48thT3QnMl/with-timestamps (model eleven_v3, stability 0.5); never sliced; laid onto the master at 0.0 s at gain 1.15 with tools/mux, no music bed. Attempt 1 (90.6 s, too slow: one-word sentences) and attempt 2 (82.8 s, a 1.48 s silence at a mid-script [dry] tag on a paragraph break) are kept beside it as take-attempt1/2.mp3.

take.max_gap_note: Measured from the audio (-40 dB, 20 ms windows on take.mp3, 2026-10-10): 1.34 s at 33.80 = the deliberate break-off beat between 'Leistungs...' and 'we'll let a German say that one.' (allowed, like N01's 1.30 s); then 1.04 s at 14.40 ('it?' -> 'Put') and 1.04 s at 26.54 ('question.' -> 'Construction'), both on chapter cuts; 0.98 s x3 (23.94, 44.60, 71.08); 15 silences are 0.8 s or longer. The approved N01, measured the same way, has 1.30 s and 1.02 s. (The alignment-based figure, 1.31 s / next 0.75 s, understated the pauses because eleven_v3's alignment folds the pause before a sentence into its first word.)

continuous_read_v3:
[dry] One tender document. Five names. Same question every time. English, schedule of quantities. Flip to Arabic and the whole page turns around. Chinese, German, Turkish. What do you call it?

Put all five on one job, and you get one thread. Prelims included? Prelims included? Prelims, in or out? Five names. One question.

Construction is the same everywhere. And vocabulary is where trust starts.

In German, Leistungs... [short pause] [amused] we'll let a German say that one. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, French, Portuguese, Vietnamese, Indonesian. Hindi just says B-O-Q. Some words travel.

Fifteen words. One document. That's the whole idea of Queue Ess Mee. Price the job in one schedule, tender that same schedule, and every bid comes back against it.

Arabic and Persian read right to left. So does the site. The sticky note doesn't.

The website speaks fifteen languages. The app speaks English, Spanish and Arabic. So far.

So, what do you call it where you work? Bonus points if you settle the prelims question. And book a thirty-minute demo at Queue Ess Mee dot build.

post_processing: Time base: start_s is time on outputs/15-languages-what-do-you-call-it-16x9.mp4 (82.1 s) = time in the take. For a line that starts a sentence after a pause it is the AUDIO-MEASURED speech onset (-40 dB, 10 ms windows on take.mp3), because eleven_v3's alignment counts the pause before a sentence as part of its first word (0.2-0.7 s early); otherwise it is the word's start in outputs/vo-take-cam-v3/alignment.json. The page was re-timed to these times (motion/15-languages-what-do-you-call-it.html v4.1, 2026-10-10), so picture follows audio: do not re-time the voice to the picture.
Mix: the whole take as ONE clip at 0.0 s, gain 1.15, no music bed (tools/mux). Output outputs/15-languages-what-do-you-call-it-16x9-with-vo.mp4 (one audio track, 82.1 s).

If the script changes, regenerate the whole take (see outputs/vo-take-cam-v3/take-text.txt for the exact text and tags), STT-check it, then re-derive every beat in the page from the new alignment and re-render.

Global video: no NZ words (tradie, GST, CCC, consent pack), no 'free' or pricing lines, no 'line by line', no app-in-15-languages claim (owner CTA rule 2026-10-03; truth sheet red list). CTA shown as qsme.build, spoken 'Queue Ess Mee dot build'.
